title: Plan, order & shop setup
summary: Lock in every option that is hard to add later, confirm the BluePrint accessory drive, and set up the shop before the truck arrives. FFR assigns a completion date at order; the SEMA special (Nov 2026) gives $2,500 off the kit or $3,500 off options.
manual: General Information chapter: tools list, torque and fluid specs.

challenges: Options that cannot be added later: IRS, power steering, A/C kit, hydraulic clutch, windows, wipers, powder coat, EFI in-tank fuel.
Pin-drive wheels do not work with the IRS (Jeff Kleiner). Stick with bolt-on Halibrands.
BluePrint's package says STOP AND CALL for Factory Five fitment: confirm the front drive carries both an A/C compressor and a PS pump.
Two TKX/IRS driveshafts are listed (60175 at 10.50" vs 16038 at 8.38"). Call FFR with the BluePrint bellhousing/TKX length.

Build order is not the manual order: 8secDuster and Papa say do the electrical, HVAC and brake lines before the engine goes in and before the outer footbox panels; once the body is on, those panels never come off. "The manual is a loose guideline."

Parts arrive late: Tiltrider1 ordered in January, got the kit in May, the harness five months later and spindles after three months on backorder. Start anyway; do not wait for a complete inventory (JimStone).

Deletes take more than you think: deleting the FFR center section also removes the spindles and hubs (PNWTim), and deleting the FFR rear brakes removes the parking-brake lines and brackets (JimStone). Ask FFR what leaves the kit with each delete before you save the money.
FFR no longer ships a printed manual (Papa, 2025: listed at $49.99 but unavailable, none in any box); print the PDF chapters you need. The mirror kit comes in some kits and not others.
ideas: Start a parts-and-cost spreadsheet like Yellville's on day one.
Take the Mk5 Roadster Build School before the kit ships; FFR says Gen 3 coupe builders take that class.
Post on the ffcars Northwest board for a Puget Sound coupe owner who will let you sit in a finished car. Seat fit and headroom cannot be judged from photos.

edwardb: "Don't build a Coupe without A/C IMO." The coupe is louder than a roadster, not daily-driver dry (leaks at the FFR windows and into the footboxes in heavy rain), and body fit is where the extra hours go.
tasks: Get a written FFR quote with every option line

Sit in a finished Gen 3 coupe (seat and headroom check)
Place the kit order and record the completion date
Start Hagerty under-construction coverage on delivery
Set up the shop: lift or stands, body dolly, bench, lighting

title: Delivery & inventory
summary: The body ships on top of the chassis and needs four people to lift off. Missing or wrong hardware is normal: photograph every box and email partsales@factoryfive.com within days. Put the MSO and every receipt in a binder; Washington's inspection depends on them.
manual: Disassembly of the Kit chapter: unboxing and parts check-off.

challenges: Backordered quarter windows and side windows are common late ships; log backorders in writing within 30 days.
The quarter-window areas of the body need the most bodywork (edwardb).
The name on the MSO must match the titling applicant. WSP requires the original.

Expect backorders on delivery day: edwardb had ~24 items short in 2017, Papa had front LCAs and the fuel tank in 2025, PNWTim found the spindles and hubs missing at inventory and had IFS shock spacers missing from two bags. Inventory takes a full day (Papa: 7 h) and the 90-day window for missing parts starts at delivery.
ideas: Build a body dolly first.
Store aluminum panels flat and labeled; they dent and oxidize in storage.

Coupe clearance is about 4": a low-profile jack, a dolly on big casters and a set of cheap 17" Mustang shop wheels (17"+ clears Wilwoods) before the kit lands. Keep parts in the numbered FFR boxes with the packing lists.
Hardware comes bagged by bolt size, not by assembly; Chris #566 re-bags it into labeled McMaster baggies per assembly before starting.
tasks: Photograph every box before opening

title: Chassis prep & aluminum panels
summary: The biggest single job: hundreds of holes drilled, cleco'd, riveted and sealed. Heat shielding, firewall insulation and footbox sealing foam go in now, before the body is on and the firewall corner fills with hoses.
manual: Chassis Assembly chapter: aluminum panel sections (floors, footboxes, firewall, trunk, cockpit sides).

reads.label: Walton Racing: rivets, clecos and rivnuts
FFR official: chassis aluminum and wiring (Dan Golub)
edwardb #59 on sealing and Sikaflex
Coupe heat management (SBF 347)
Sealing the cabin (ffcars 617986)
Panel order, regulator mount, tap vs rivnut (new forum 136789)
MSumners' log: test-fit the drivetrain before powder coat

challenges: Silicone vs Sikaflex debate; panels oxidize if uncoated, so coat them before the pedal box and wiring go in.
Most cockpit heat is engine-bay air pushed along the footbox-to-body gap, not conduction. Seal it with dense foam before the body goes on.
Dropped floors for tall drivers must be decided before panels are riveted.

Leave the engine-bay and radiator-area aluminum off until the engine is in (except the footbox insides and fronts). Trans side panels go on after the floor and share rivets. Test-fit every panel before cutting or bending: one misplaced panel opens gaps three panels later (Papa).

Tap the frame or use rivnuts on the top footbox panels so the HVAC and wiring behind them can be serviced; the passenger footbox panel is sealed in place and the outer panels cannot come off with the body on (8secDuster, FitzHappens).

If the frame is going to powder coat, test-fit the engine and transmission and drill the panels first: MSumners had to remove the tunnel cross brace for the trans tail and modify brackets, and PNWTim cut the steering-rack bracket relief, all before coating. Prismatic Stone Black survived a 6-hour gasoline soak (MSumners).
ideas: Satin clear over aluminum (jgray) for a finished look at low cost.
Standoff aluminum heat shield with an air gap at the headers.
Avoid tar-based mats near heat; they melt and make a sticky mess.
tasks: Inspect powder coat; touch up bare spots
Fit, drill and cleco every aluminum panel
Install footbox heat shields and firewall insulation
Seal the footbox-to-body gap with dense foam
Rivet and seal panels (Sikaflex every seam)
Spray or lay sound deadening before carpet areas close

title: Front suspension, steering, pedals & brakes
summary: KONI coil-overs, the Wilwood pedal box and the steering column go in while the footbox is open. Decide power steering, quick-release wheel and pedal spacing now. FFR itself says you will want power steering once you try manual.
manual: Chassis Assembly: front suspension, steering rack and column, pedal box, brake lines.

reads.label: Walton Racing: front suspension
FFR official: front Wilwood install
Low Boost Films: Wilwood pedal box install
Quick release + Russ Thompson turn signal
Widen the pedal box? Pedal offset and Snakebite extensions
Koni DA snap rings do not fit (leave off or spiral ring)

challenges: Accelerator pedal vs steering-shaft interference (Bob Brandle made a spacer); throttle pedal wobble (jgray).
Standard 500 lb front springs may be light if the finished car tops 2,900 lb.
A cast Wilwood clutch pedal broke on a roadster with a cable clutch; hydraulic lowers the load.

The pedals sit left of the seat centerline in every coupe. edwardb and 8secDuster: a non-issue you adapt to; angle the seats, move the Wilwood pads, and leave the footbox alone until the headers are in. 8secDuster's real problem was clutch/brake pad spacing.
A column-mounted turn-signal switch moves the wheel 2"+ closer to the driver (Gordon Levy); a turn-signal timer on a toggle keeps the wheel where it is for a tall driver.

Wilwood rotor hat bolts torque to 155 inch-pounds with red Loctite; jdavis500 snapped one reading it as foot-pounds. The kit Mevotech upper ball joints did not fit for edwardb, Papa or PNWTim: order Howe 22320S with the kit.
ideas: Dead-pedal kit and rigid stainless brake lines (edwardb).
Bench-bleed, then pressure-bleed at 5–7 psi.

Install KONI coil-overs and front sway bar
Mount the pedal box; set pedal height and dead pedal

title: Rear suspension (IRS) & rear brakes
summary: The 2015 Mustang-based IRS is the street choice: smoother ride, better traction, and nearly impossible to retrofit. It needs its own shocks (17150), the 2018 3.55 center section (16668) and the matching driveshaft.
manual: Chassis Assembly: rear suspension (IRS supplement), e-brake.

reads.label: The Roadster Experience: FFR IRS install (same IRS as the coupe)
FFR official: rear Wilwood install
Yellville: rear Wilwood brakes
Grassroots Motorsports Gen 3 race build (IRS assembly)
IRS frame rub with 315s: spacer, camber or notch
Rear sway bar on a coupe with IRS (brackets, snap oversteer)
JimStone's log: Wilwoods from Summit, what the brake delete removes

challenges: IRS bushing misalignment needs spacers; drill spindle and mount holes to 5/8".
Pinion flange adapter error that FFR replaced (P100DHG #138).
Ask about 3.73 vs 3.55 for the TKX 0.81 overdrive.
315s on the IRS rub the frame behind the passenger seat: 1" spacer and -0.5° camber on a street car (edwardb, 11k miles); notch and re-weld the channel on a track car (Jphoenix).

Measure the driveline angle with a digital gauge before the engine goes in: burchfieldb's IRS mount pointed down about 0.5° and needed custom bushings. Install the diff before the engine test-fit; the pinion angle can rotate (edwardb). The IRS driveline sits 1–1.5" right of center by design.

Rear hubs come with metric studs. Drive them out (PNWTim: 1" black-pipe crib and the vise anvil) and press 1/2-20 studs; if spacers are planned, use the shorter Dorman 610-364 studs. Tight toe/UCA tabs spread with an 18" adjustable wrench; the 95-lb diff goes in with an engine hoist (Chris #566).
ideas: Electric parking brake (Levy Racing / Wilwood EPB) frees the tunnel.
Torque-seal every fastener for the inspector.
tasks: Assemble IRS cradle, knuckles and hubs

Install rear coil-overs and sway bar

Torque-seal every fastener

challenges: TKX shifter position; several builders flipped the shifter and moved the tunnel hole.
Oil pan clearance (rear-sump), tall intakes hit the hood, degas/overflow tank location.
The 4-into-2-into-sidepipe routing is a reported power robber; GAS-N's design has a longer, more gradual turn.

TKX shifter, Oct 2026: with a Coyote, edwardb flips the shifter 180° to the rear position and skips the mid-shift kit; gtrag94: "for a SBF you DO want the midshift position" (the small square plate forward of the normal mount). PNWTim: set the shifter before you raise the tailshaft and fit the crossmember; there is no room after.

GAS-N headers and pipes are a roll of the dice in 2025–26 (tabs welded in the wrong place, months-long waits); JimStone's FFR stainless set was a perfect fit. Quiet FFR pipes with Car Chemistry inserts, or go Boig.

BluePrint shipped mtdr's 427/TKX "mid-shift package" with the shifter in the normal rear position because Tremec had no mid-shift available; flipping the plate 180° gains 4–5" and needs one piece of tunnel bracing removed (mdjr70). Ask BluePrint what position the TKX will actually arrive in.
ideas: Ceramic headers and standoff heat shields; bare FFR pipes rust fast in Washington.
Fan shroud (Breeze 70807) for low-speed and A/C idle cooling.
Driveshaft safety loop on rivnuts.
Jphoenix runs standard FFR roadster side pipes on a street Type 65 (302 + GAS-N headers) with a custom support bracket: under 102 dB at Portland and 103 dB at every PNW track.

title: Wiring, fuel, hydraulics & gauges
summary: Ron Francis harness, in-tank EFI pump, hydraulic clutch and brake lines, battery in the nose. Plan the crowded firewall corner where harness, heater hoses and A/C lines all meet.
manual: Chassis Assembly: wiring harness, fuel tank and EFI in-tank pump, radiator and fan, clutch hydraulics, gauges.

challenges: BluePrint ECU/injector data mismatch (lewma); a wrong control pack cost Walton Racing months.
The Sniper 1 internal regulator is a known failure point; Sniper 2 needs a separate regulator and 3/8" lines.
GPS gauge part number differs between the order form (60312) and catalog (60311).

The kit's 5/16" supply and 1/4" return are small for EFI: Papa runs 3/8" both ways with a Trick Flow filter at the tunnel; Holley asks for 3/8". Check filter ports (NPT vs ORB) before buying adapters: two builders had Russell/Evil Energy fittings seat only two turns.
Throttle cable: cut the swaged end off the kit cable and use a swivel connector at the pedal, or buy a Lokar (Papa). You drill the firewall hole yourself.
ideas: Keyless push-button start, all-LED lighting with electronic flashers, GPS speedometer, laser-etched switch panel (edwardb).
Door-pocket phone chargers (Rocky R.), one aux lead straight to the battery for a tender.

summary: Space behind the Gen 3 dash is tight; edwardb concluded the FFR kit (Siroco Boreal 600) is the best and maybe only solution. As delivered it has two always-on outlets and no defrost diverter. Washington rain plus the WSP defroster check makes this the biggest comfort and inspection risk.

rickster991 (BP 347 EFI + PS + A/C): the evaporator fittings backed off twice (Loctite them), the heater hoses leaked onto the passenger at high revs, and nothing on the heater side can be reached with the body on. If starting over he would skip the firewall fittings and put the hose connections where the evaporator can come out. Install heat and A/C before riveting the passenger footbox (Papa, Sea Hut).
ideas: Y-connections feeding 2 defrost + 4 dash outlets (ffcars builder, 4+ seasons without fogging).
Tint the hatch glass; heated seat pads (30-minute install).
Papa uses the FFR coolant overflow tank as the washer reservoir; Bob Brandle moves the overflow forward of the engine because under the cowl you cannot see or fill it.

title: Body fit: doors, hood, hatch, windows, lights
summary: The coupe-specific job: door gaps, hatch glass, roof line and side windows take far longer than on a roadster. Bodies vary up to 1/2" side to side. Set hatch glass height and door gaps before paint.
manual: Body chapter: mounting, door hinges and latches, hood, hatch and glass, side windows, wipers, lights, bumpers.

reads.label: John Nizman: body fit and hatch glass
John Nizman: side glass and brackets
Rear hatch alignment
Side window question (frames differ side to side)
Door latch reliability
Tim Custer: Forma power window kit install
Kevin's Garage: setting the body (Mk4, transfers)
Body fitting – Type 65 Coupe: 120 replies, Sep–Nov 2026 (PNWTim)
Spoiler mounted from below through a slot (TwinFins)
Side glass: pay a glass shop (Kleiner, David Williamson)
Which hatch panels can be on when the body goes on (ffcars)

challenges: Plastic latch housings crack; add door poppers as a backup and metal handles.
Hood hinge bracket clearance; hatch glass high at the corners (use a temporary D-seal to save the FFR strip).
No Gen 3 builder has documented a fully weather-tight coupe. Plan on FormaCars windows or careful sealing.

Hood hinge brackets have had the wrong geometry since Gen 1: 3D-printed wedge (~1/2" over 5-7/8"), or cut and re-weld the bracket (Build School), or ask FFR for the revised hinges that 2025 kits (Lugnut Mark #686) came with. Measure: 83.5° and 98° were both seen.

Sills: the fiberglass sill must sit flush on the frame tube; bodies are not symmetrical, so notch the body or grind the lower cross-tube ends, push in and down, clamp, and screw in three places. Sill glass varies from 1/4" to a few mm at the rear; build up the thin spots (JimStone).

Nose and hood: the nose is asymmetric and sits off-center 1/2–3/4" on most cars and cannot be moved sideways; "put the ruler away" (Kleiner). Trim the back edge of the nose in small steps so the hinge brackets reach the cups, raise the front with the heim joint to get the hood parallel, leave the gas struts off until it fits. Notch the nose underside for the A/C condenser and radiator; a 1/2" gap to the shroud seal is normal. edwardb spent two full weeks on body fit: hood → body → doors, repeat.

Doors: both are too long for the opening; trim both ends (Indy Shu trimmed only the front and ended up with 3–4 washers under the striker). The driver door often will not sit flush: 1/8–1/4" spacers between frame and skin. Kleiner relieves the radius on the upper hinge for more swing on every coupe; the 1/4" in the manual means 1/4". Doors are harder than the nose.

Nose latches: swap the supplied 10-32 hardware for 1/4-20 (edwardb, PNWTim). Headlight bucket cutouts came badly undersized: open with a carbide burr. The body settles and fits better after a few days on the frame.

Hatch side panels can be on the chassis when the body is set, but the rear splash shield (#42) and the panels behind the seats (#11) go in only after the body is on for the last time (Jeff Kleiner, dougstelter).
ideas: Nose pop-up mod with a BMW E30 hood latch (ffr48).
Quick-release wheel for easier entry; roof NACA ducts if you skip A/C.

Side glass: Kleiner and David Williamson both paid an independent auto-glass shop to set the side windows ("not expensive, worth it"; Safelite declined). FFR's gasket-roll tool and instructions have errors.

title: Title in gelcoat (Washington)
summary: Title before paint so the deadline does not depend on the paint shop. Kit vehicle under RCW 46.12.695: WSP VIN inspection by appointment with the MSO, original receipts, a certified weight slip and the licensing-agent request form. No emissions test in Washington since 2020.
manual: Not in the FFR manual. See the WSP kit vehicle guide and the titling section of the build plan.

reads.label: WSP Kit Vehicle Inspection Guide (PDF)

Jphoenix: WA licensed a 289 FIA with no bumpers; tax invoiced on kit + engine only

challenges: Online WSP slots fill in seconds; call the local WSP office. Allow 1–3 months.

Use tax is owed at titling on anything you did not pay Washington sales tax on (~$4,000 in one case). Most big remote sellers collect WA tax at checkout now; private-party and small-shop buys usually don't. Keep every receipt with the tax line visible; the hub's tax-paid flag tracks it.

Bumpers: the WSP checklist lists them, but RCW 46.37.518 makes hoods and bumpers optional on kit vehicles. Make sure the car goes through as a kit vehicle (RCW 46.12.695), not an assembled vehicle, and bring the statute.
ideas: Print RCW 46.37.518 and RCW 46.12.695 for the inspection folder.
Register as a collector vehicle; ask for the 1965 model-year precedent.
Order the extra side mirror (12079X/15834X) for the inspection.

Jphoenix licensed an FIA roadster in Washington with no bumpers: WSP accepted "steel frame inside body". His licensing office invoiced use tax on the kit and the engine/transmission only, not every receipt.
